title: Open Tree of Life web services
note: Topology and taxonomy context; divergence dates require separate evidence.

title: Evolutionary Origin of the Turtle Shell
authors: Lyson, T.R.; Bever, G.S.; Scheyer, T.M.; Hsiang, A.Y.; Gauthier, J.A.
note: The study describes multiple Eunotosaurus specimens and histological sections, including NHM PV R 4949 and SAM K 1133; its stem-turtle placement and shell sequence are character-matrix and homology interpretations.

title: A Middle Triassic stem-turtle and the evolution of the turtle body plan
note: The Vellberg sample includes SMNS 91356, SMNS 91360 and SMNS 92066; robust paired gastralia and broadened ribs are observations, while serial fusion and Pan-Testudines placement are interpretations.

title: An ancestral turtle from the Late Triassic of southwestern China
authors: Li, C.; Wu, X.-C.; Rieppel, O.; Wang, L.-T.; Zhao, L.-J.
note: Holotype IVPP V 15639, paratype IVPP V 13240 and referred specimen IVPP V 15653 document a plastron and incomplete dorsal shell; topology, habitat and assembly sequence are bounded interpretations.

title: A Divergence Dating Analysis of Turtles Using Fossil Calibrations: An Example of Best Practices
authors: Joyce, W.G.; Parham, J.F.; Lyson, T.R.; Warnock, R.C.M.; Donoghue, P.C.J.
note: Node 1 uses Caribemys oxfordiensis holotype MNHNCu P-3209 for a 155.6 Ma hard minimum and a 251.4 Ma soft maximum; posterior crown ages are model outputs, not specimen dates.

title: A Triassic stem lepidosaur illuminates the origin of lizard-like reptiles
authors: Martínez, R.N.; Simões, T.R.; Sobral, G.; Apesteguía, S.
note: Holotype PVSJ 698 is a three-dimensionally preserved skull from the Ischigualasto Formation; CT anatomy is direct evidence and stem-lepidosauromorph placement is a multi-analysis result.

title: The origin of squamates revealed by a Middle Triassic lizard from the Italian Alps
authors: Simões, T.R.; Caldwell, M.W.; Tałanda, M.; et al.
note: Holotype and only specimen PZO 628 was analysed by high-resolution micro-CT and a combined morphological-molecular matrix; CT data are archived at DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4157321.

title: Synchrotron tomography of a stem lizard elucidates early squamate anatomy
authors: Tałanda, M.; Fernandez, V.; Panciroli, E.; Evans, S.E.; et al.
note: NMS G.2022.1.1 was scanned at ESRF ID19 and scored with referred dentaries and Kirtlington material; the molecular-backbone Bayesian analyses recover Bellairsia on the squamate stem.

title: A Triassic crown squamate
authors: Whiteside, D.I.; Chambi-Trowell, S.A.V.; Benton, M.J.
note: The paper describes holotype NHMUK PV R36822 and referred fissure-fill material and recovers Cryptovaranoides inside crown Squamata; data are archived at DOI 10.5061/dryad.hhmgqnkkr.

title: The affinities of the Late Triassic Cryptovaranoides and the age of crown squamates
authors: Brownstein, C.D.; Simões, T.R.; Caldwell, M.W.; Lee, M.S.Y.; Meyer, D.L.; Scarpetta, S.G.
note: The authors revise anatomical scorings and referral assumptions and recover Cryptovaranoides as an archosauromorph or indeterminate neodiapsid in tested matrices.

title: Late Triassic Cryptovaranoides microlanius is a squamate, not an archosauromorph
authors: Whiteside, D.I.; Chambi-Trowell, S.A.V.; Benton, M.J.
note: The response restricts conservative scoring to holotype or directly referable elements and retains a crown-squamate interpretation; disputed referrals and character identities remain explicit.

title: Cryptovaranoides is not a squamate
authors: Caldwell, M.W.; Brownstein, C.D.; Meyer, D.L.; Scarpetta, S.G.; Lee, M.S.Y.; Simões, T.R.
note: This further reassessment challenges anatomical codings, referrals and analytical replication; the competing crown-squamate placement remains unresolved in this package.

title: Inferring weak spots in phylogenetic trees: application to mosasauroid nomenclature
note: Table 1 gives explicit phylogenetic definitions for Mosasauroidea and Mosasauridae; sensitivity analyses retain uncertainty around basal branching.

title: Dallasaurus turneri, a new primitive mosasauroid from the Middle Turonian of Texas and comments on the phylogeny of Mosasauridae (Squamata)
note: Two incomplete skeletons from middle Turonian deposits of north-central Texas preserve plesiopedal limbs; family placement and locomotor specialization are distinct questions.
